# The British Empire at its largest, 1920

The British Empire was at its largest just after the First World War. Around 1920 it covered about 35.5 million square kilometres, by the usual estimate, roughly a quarter of the world's land. In 1913 it had ruled about 412 million people, close to a quarter of the world's population.

The war added territory. Under League of Nations mandates Britain took over Palestine, Transjordan and Iraq from the Ottoman Empire, and Tanganyika and parts of Togoland and Cameroon from Germany. The dominions took mandates of their own: South Africa took South West Africa, and Australia and New Zealand took German possessions in the Pacific.

It was not one kind of rule. Canada, Australia, New Zealand, South Africa and Newfoundland were self-governing dominions. India was ruled by a British administration. Many smaller territories were colonies or protectorates.

The peak did not last long. Most of Ireland left the United Kingdom as the Irish Free State in 1922, and Britain declared Egypt independent the same year. The atlas draws the whole empire in one colour, so the map shows how far it reached.

## On the map

Areas as the atlas draws them on its 1920 CE chart:

- United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland: about 34.6 million km²
- France: about 12.4 million km²
- Soviet Russia (RSFSR): about 19.4 million km²
- United States: about 9.6 million km²

These are the atlas's own measurements of its own borders, so they can differ from the published estimates in the text. Borders before the modern era are an interpretation. Every realm on the chart is listed on the year page for 1920 CE.
